title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: reading whether every original is back before a corrected set
content:
## Scope

This rule of the Bills of Lading and Transport Documents product explains how the desk reads whether all originals of the previous set have come back to the line, at the moment a corrected transport document is issued as a new set after a correction that required the originals back.

## Formal clause

1. The reading uses the document's own recorded figure of originals still in circulation, as it stands at the moment the corrected set is issued.
2. The originals count as all back only when that figure is 0.
3. A figure of 1 or more means that originals of the previous set are still in circulation, so the originals are not all back.

## Input and judgement

| Recorded figure of originals still in circulation on the document | Judgement |
|---|---|
| 0 | All originals are back |
| 1 or more | Not all originals are back |

## Hypothetical cases

The figures are invented for illustration.

- A previous set of 3 originals, of which 3 have been lodged back with the line: the recorded figure reads 0, so all originals are back.
- A previous set of 3 originals, of which 2 have been lodged back: the recorded figure reads 1, so the originals are not all back.

## Points of judgement

- **Question:** At which moment is the figure read? **Answer:** As the document stands at the moment the corrected set is issued, not as it stood when the correction was requested.
- **Question:** The customer says every original was handed in. **Answer:** The judgement follows the figure recorded on the document; only a recorded figure of 0 means all originals are back.
